Hi Peter / Soojin,

Quick technical breakdown to make the mapping explicit — examples below use approximate token counts from the attached sample rows. I kept the math simple so procurement can see the delta.

Summary (short):
- Responses endpoint: billed on a single unified unit — input tokens + output tokens are both counted, and we apply the hosted Responses price per 1K tokens. It was designed to be cheaper for short-turnaround single-response requests because we optimize context encoding.
- Chat Completions: billed per-message aggregation. Each user+assistant message pair is tokenized and billed; long multi-turn contexts can increase input token counts because we include full dialogue history. Price per 1K tokens is slightly higher on Chat historically due to longer context overhead in runtime.
- Legacy Completions (old API): billed per completion output tokens + prompt tokens. It behaves similarly to Responses in token accounting but lacks some batching and KV cache optimizations, so effective cost per served prompt can be higher if you have many short prompts.

Example mapping (from your sample):
- Sample row A: 18 input tokens, 120 output tokens, single-turn lookup
  * Responses billing: counts 138 tokens -> billed_units = 0.138 (in thousands)
  * Chat billing: counts full message pair (same tokens) but chat pricing multiplier ~1.05 on hosted plans for multi-message bookkeeping -> billed_units_effective ~= 0.145
  * Legacy Completions: billed = 138 tokens but runtime inefficiencies make effective cost similar to Chat for short prompts

- Sample row B: 640 input tokens (product context), 1,200 output tokens (long description)
  * Responses billing: 1,840 tokens -> 1.840 units (1K token units)
  * Chat billing: if using multi-turn (3 messages) history included, you can see 2,200+ tokens -> ~2.2 units billed
  * Legacy Completions: 1.84 units billed but higher per-unit price often applies if run at scale without caching/quantization

Discount / commit guidance (hosted):
- Standard hosted list: $0.018 / 1K tokens for Responses, $0.021 / 1K for Chat Completions, Legacy varies by model and often routes to the higher of the two. (These are illustrative; see attached ratecard PDF for full matrix.)
- Commit bands (annual prepaid spend):
  * $100k+ -> 10% discount off hosted list + 30% reserved throughput burst credit
  * $500k+ -> 18% discount + 50% burst credit + guaranteed latency SLO bump
  * $1M+ -> 25% discount + custom routing policies and dedicated capacity options
- Note: discounts are negotiable by deal with some flexibility on how we treat Responses vs Chat buckets (we can normalize both to Responses pricing at negotiation stage if helpful).

Bursting: hosted customers can enable a "burst bucket" (pay-as-you-go, pre-provisioned credit) to absorb spikes. If you commit to a band we can increase the burst buffer automatically over holiday windows.

I'm attaching the current hosted ratecard (redwood-ratecard-Q3.pdf) and a one-page mapping doc I'll drop into the drive.

If you want, Jordan can run a quick cost-sensitivity spreadsheet during the call Thursday to show cost under three migration options (stay on legacy, migrate to Responses, or hybrid with caching).
